bull.t: Rapid Revenue Growth And Strong Unit Economics
bull.b: CoreWeave is scaling rapidly while retaining high gross and EBITDA margins, indicating attractive economics in its GPU cloud model. If demand remains strong, this combination can support operating leverage and improve the company’s ability to fund expansion over the next several quarters.

bull.t: Large Backlog, Pricing Power, And Demand Visibility
bull.b: A large, growing backlog and demonstrated pricing increases provide unusually strong revenue visibility for a capacity-constrained infrastructure provider. These commitments can support sustained growth and margin resilience, while excess qualified demand strengthens CoreWeave’s negotiating position with customers.

bull.t: Expansion Of Managed AI Infrastructure Products
bull.b: Managed inference adoption adds a recurring software-enabled service layer to CoreWeave’s GPU infrastructure offering. Its early booked revenue and capacity-constrained growth suggest customers are using more than basic compute, potentially broadening monetization and increasing platform relevance over time.

bear.b: Extreme leverage leaves CoreWeave with limited balance-sheet cushion if growth slows, customer commitments change, or financing conditions worsen. Large debt obligations also restrict capital-allocation flexibility and make execution of the expansion plan more sensitive to operating and funding outcomes.

bear.t: Deeply Negative And Worsening Free Cash Flow
bear.b: Operating cash flow is substantial, but investment spending currently consumes far more cash, producing deeply negative free cash flow. Until capital intensity moderates or returns improve, CoreWeave remains dependent on financing, prepayments, and successful execution to sustain its growth program.

bear.t: Net Losses And Rising Interest Burden
bear.b: Growing losses alongside sharply higher interest expense show that strong revenue and adjusted margins have not yet translated into bottom-line profitability. This burden can absorb more operating cash, constrain reinvestment, and delay financial resilience while the company continues its capital-intensive buildout.
